subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: What Telegram behavior should OpenClaw own when a voice message is much older than dispatch time and the resulting run aborts before a visible reply?
rationale: The source confirms missing instrumentation, but threshold, restart/alert policy, and direct-message fallback semantics are user-visible reliability decisions that should not be guessed by automation.

options.title: Keep open for maintainer-defined watchdog and fallback
options.body: Choose a bounded source-age diagnostic/watchdog and aborted/no-final fallback contract, then require focused tests plus live Telegram proof before closing.

options.title: Split the symptoms into narrower canonical items
options.body: Track ingress-latency handling separately from recovery-turn delivery so #86541 and #91652 can land independently without claiming to fix this whole report.

options.title: Close as covered by adjacent work
options.body: Only choose this if maintainers decide #86541 plus #91652 together are the intended canonical coverage despite the missing source-age watchdog evidence.

recommendation.title: Keep open for maintainer-defined watchdog and fallback
recommendation.body: Choose a bounded source-age diagnostic/watchdog and aborted/no-final fallback contract, then require focused tests plus live Telegram proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The most direct current code path is Telegram polling liveness, where this history points first, while delivery fallback owners remain adjacent.
